title: First called Christians (Acts 11)
hookLine: a well-known sentence with a blank in it: called Christians, by whom?
tomorrow: how does a man sleep the night before his trial?

cards: Nicknames are rarely chosen. A teammate says one once, it sticks, and years later it's written on a birthday cake.
Acts has a sentence like that, and it's well-known: "And the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch." Now read it again, slowly. Called by whom?
The sentence has no one doing the calling. Somebody handed the believers the name, and Acts leaves the somebody blank. So where did it come from, and what was in it?

teach.b: Start with who was there. After Stephen's death, believers scatter, and Acts says they share the word with Jews only.

Then some men of Cyprus and Cyrene reach Antioch and start talking to Greeks as well, "And the hand of the Lord was with them." A new, mixed community starts meeting in a big city. Jerusalem sends Barnabas to look.
When he "had seen the grace of God, was glad." He goes to Tarsus to find Saul and brings him back, and for a whole year the two of them teach there. Then the name.
Here's the honest answer to the puzzle: the text doesn't say who coined it, and anyone who tells you for certain is reading outside Acts. What the text does give is the name's core.
Christian is built on Christ, and a chapter earlier Peter had said what that title meant to them: "God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power."

teach.h: FIRST THING THEY DID: A COLLECTION.
teach.b: Some readers hear an even smaller name inside it: little christs, people carrying his name down a city street where the neighbors can see whether it fits.
And the very next scene shows what the named people did. A prophet named Agabus warns of a famine, so the disciples, "every man according to his ability," send relief to the believers in Judaea.
The name arrives, and the first thing they do with it is take up a collection.

how: Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant churches use the name Christian; Acts 11:26 is where the name appears in the story, first in Antioch.

o: a Roman word for people who refused to fight
a name given in Antioch, built on Christ
a title the apostles chose at the Last Supper

p: where they were first called Christians
saw the grace of God, was glad

s: the disciples chose the name Christian for themselves
Acts says they were called Christians, and never says who called them.
Barnabas went to Tarsus to find Saul
and the two of them taught in Antioch for a whole year.
the Antioch believers sent relief to Judaea, each as he was able
every man according to his ability: their first act after the name.

games.q: kids at school start calling your friend group 'the church kids,' and it sticks. what does Antioch suggest?
o: let the name push you to live up to it, the way Antioch took up a collection.
make them stop; a name you didn't choose can't mean anything.
drift from the group so the label doesn't follow you around.
games.why: the believers didn't pick their name. they were called Christians, and the next thing Acts shows is them sending relief, every man according to his ability.

practice: Say your own name out loud, once, slowly. Then say one word you'd hope people hear in it when you're not in the room: kind, honest, steady.
Sit with the space between the two without judging it, and say your name once more at the end.

wordCard.voice: Christian. A name the disciples were given in Antioch, built on Christ, the anointed one.

orig.note: Greek: Christians, the word in Acts 11:26, called Christians first in Antioch.

carryVoice: The line for today: little christs, a name they were handed and had to grow into. Day done.
